newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Wolseley cautious after profits rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Wolseley cautious after profits rise.

text.p: International building supplies distributor Wolseley Plc announced a 12 percent rise in first-half profits on Tuesday but sounded a cautious note for the rest of the year.
Pretax profits for the six months to January 31 rose 12 percent to 124.3 million pounds ($197.2 million) on sales up 9.8 percent at 2.28 billion pounds.
The interim dividend was increased to 3.3 pence from 3.1 pence on earnings up nine percent at 14.63p a share.
But the company, which counts the United States as its biggest single market, warned that results for the rest of the year would be hit by sterling's recent strength.
Currency translations wiped 79.1 million pounds off reported turnover and 4.2 million pounds off profits in the first six months.

"The effect in the first half was 4.2 million pounds; in the second half it is likely to be more than 4.2 million if exchange rates ramain at these levels," finance director Steven Webster told reporters.
Chairman Richard Ireland also sounded a cautious note on trading, saying that there was little change in prospect for conditions in its European and U.S. markets for the rest of the year.

But the share price was held steady around 496-1/2 pence after investors had digested the results, against an overall weaker market, on the view that the company had been unduly cautious in its results statement.
"It was a bit of a mixed message really," said Robin hardy of broker Panmure Gordon. "I think the word cautious was used more times than it was meant."

Ireland said 12 months of strong growth in its all-important U.S. business was now likely to level off, British markets were only picking up slowly and little relief could be expected this year from the depressed economies in France and Austria, it's two other main markets.

"The upturn in the UK housing market remains fragile and is unlikely to deliver much benefit...until later in the year," he said. "Consumers may be reluctant to increase expenditure to any great extent until after the election (on May 1)."

But the U.S. distribution business, Wolseley's biggest market, proved buoyant in the first half, with trading profits up 21.7 percent at 56.6 million pounds on a 14.6 percent increase in sales to 1.2 billion pounds.

Like-for-like sales in U.S. distribution before acquisitions were up 10.3 percent and profits up 16.1 percent. Ireland said U.S. business conditions were strong although housebuilding starts had slowed recently and it was likely that the rate of growth would slow during the second half relative to the upturn in the equivalent period last year.

The company said there had been some pressure on margins in its fast-growing U.S. timber distribution and joinery businesses but chief executive John Young said they were still making good profits. "Margins are still under pressure but they are acceptable margins...we are very happy with the returns we get from these businesses," he told reporters.

And he said the company would continue to make bolt-on acquisitions to expand its U.S. and European distribution networks. Net borrowings at the end of January stood at 109.6 million pounds, up 49.8 million pounds on a year ago, to give a debt to equity gearing of 13.3 percent. In the first six months the company spent 70.7 million pounds on acquisitions, including 43.2 million pounds on deals in the U.S. "The modest gearing ratio provides ample flexibility in this respect," Ireland said.
